speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me; please describe your chronic left shoulder pain, including exactly where it hurts and what activities make it worse. To start our evaluation, have you noticed any limitations in your range of motion, such as difficulty reaching behind your back?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Adhesive Capsulitis (Frozen Shoulder). The clinical picture of insidious onset, progressive pain limiting all active and likely passive range of motion in a diabetic patient with no trauma or neurologic deficits is classic for this condition. REQUEST IMAGES: Left_Shoulder_MRI.
